basis: Acquired C1-inhibitor deficiency causes subcutaneous angioedema; episodic gut and airway swelling does not establish lasting organ damage.
APOA1 amyloidosis: renal failure 2/2, heart failure 5/5, hepatic amyloid 3/3 with failure reported; cutaneous amyloidosis omitted by cap.
A stromal corneal dystrophy; ocular location defines the disease despite usually preserved vision.
Tumor originates in the CNS meninges; pericytic differentiation does not establish systemic vascular disease.
Hereditary TTR amyloid disorder defined by myocardial infiltration; neuropathy and other extracardiac damage are below 30% in supplied annotations.
Factor IX deficiency; recurrent joint/muscle bleeding is annotated 80-99% and damages joints. Intracranial hemorrhage is clinically a minority across severity groups.
Congenital limb dysostosis involving tibial development, digit number and skeletal fusion.
Primary breast carcinoma; breast has no axis, and metastatic disease is not intrinsic to this concept.
Corneal stromal lipid deposition defines the ocular condition; it does not itself establish a systemic lipid disorder.
Muscle dystrophy with contractures; sustained respiratory failure from diaphragmatic weakness and esotropia are each annotated frequent (30-79%).
Autoimmune thrombotic coagulopathy; renal microangiopathic injury occurs in ~70%. Pulmonary (~60%) and CNS (~55%) injury omitted by cap.
Immune-mediated psoriasis of the skin; an infectious trigger does not establish additional organ involvement.
Heavy-chain amyloidosis; nephropathy 80-99%, cardiac amyloid 30-79%. Nerve deposition alone is insufficient; functional neuropathy is annotated only 5-29%.
Neoplasm confined by definition to the breast ductal system; breast has no axis.
Inherited proximal tubulopathy with proteinuria, hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis; rickets and osteomalacia affect a minority.
Fibrosing interstitial myositis affects skeletal muscle; the definition does not establish an autoimmune or infectious mechanism.
Nephronophthisis and hepatic fibrosis define the syndrome; retinal and neurodevelopmental involvement is not established in at least 30%.
Ear malformations 80-99%; oral clefts and ocular malformations 30-79%. Toenail hypoplasia affects 30-79%; skeletal findings omitted by cap.
CLDN14-related nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss; no syndromic extra-auditory disease is established.
Congenital cleft of the upper lip and tooth-bearing maxillary alveolar bone; external nasal shape changes do not establish airway injury.
Corrosive chloroacetate causes chemical burns and systemic metabolic toxicity with acidosis; common lasting CNS or cardiac damage is not established.
Combined immunodeficiency with lymphopenia and neutropenia; eczema affects roughly half of reported cases. Recurrent infections alone do not prove other organ damage.
Multiple bony exostoses and neurologic spastic tetraparesis jointly define the syndrome.
The definition describes acute iron poisoning with direct corrosive gastrointestinal injury; hepatic necrosis, shock and severe acidosis occur mainly in severe cases.
IL6R-related immunodeficiency; intrinsic atopic dermatitis occurs in 2/2 patients. Recurrent ear and respiratory infections do not establish lasting organ damage.
